bai.moTa: Sample an electron cloud and compare the 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals.
bai.yChinh: An orbital describes a quantum state. The point cloud samples repeated position measurements. Its shape and nodes are set by the wave function.
bai.giaiThich: This nonrelativistic hydrogen model uses a fixed nucleus and Coulomb attraction. Dots sample all space; the ring marks a test radius in Bohr radii.
bai.conSo.2: Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n²: 1s lies at −13.6 eV; 2s and 2p both lie at −3.4 eV, 1/4 of the 1s energy.
bai.conSo.3: Bohr radius a₀ ≈ 0.0529 nm. The radial distribution peaks exactly at a₀ for 1s and at 4a₀ for 2p.
bai.hieuDung: The colors of the 2p lobes indicate the signs of its real wave function. The electron charge is the same in both lobes.
bai.nguon: Prepared by Trí Lữ. OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, `8.1; Griffiths and Schroeter, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Ch. 4.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.1: Distinguish local density and radial distribution.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.4: Use the quantum numbers n and l to count nodes and read the energy Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n².
bai.baiGiang.buoc.1.noiDung:
Each dot records an electron position from an atom prepared in the same state. The nucleus is at the center. Rotate to see the cloud in depth. Rate-limited clicks represent sampled detections.

Rotate before comparing two regions by eye. Dots in front of the nucleus can overlap those behind it in a two-dimensional projection. Apparent brightness depends on depth. The adjacent graph answers a different question by adding contributions from all directions at a given radius.

$$ P(dV)=|\psi|^2dV $$

+++ A closer look · Read a small volume
Of two equal small volumes, the denser one has the higher average count.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Resample|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.noiDung:
The local 1s density decreases away from the nucleus. At a fixed radius its wave function is independent of direction.

Place the radius ring near the cloud core and rotate. The ring is a horizontal section of a test sphere; points with that radius can lie above or below it. There is no sharp outer edge enclosing all possible positions.

$$ |\psi_{1s}|^2=e^{-2r/a_0}/(\pi a_0^3) $$

+++ A closer look · A finite point cloud
Random gaps between a few dots are insufficient evidence of a node. Look for deficits that persist across samples.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Select 1s|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.noiDung:
A distant thin shell encloses more volume than a nearer shell of equal thickness. Thus the 1s radial distribution peaks at finite radius although local density peaks at the center.

A small detector at the center records more than an equal-volume detector far away. With two shells of equal thickness, also count how many small detectors fit in each. Regrouping measurements alone changes the location of the maximum.

$$ P_{1s}(r)=4r^2e^{-2r/a_0}/a_0^3 $$

+++ A closer look · Find the maximum
The derivative vanishes at one Bohr radius; the distribution rises before that point and falls after it. The gold graph shows radial probability density. The Bohr radius is $a_0=4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar^2/(m_e e^2)\approx0{,}0529$ nm, about one twentieth of a nanometre.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Choose ground state|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.de: Drag the radius probe to the 1s maximum within 0.12a₀.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.goiY: Use the gold graph and the r/a₀ readout.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.noiDung:
Switch to 2s. The cloud remains spherically symmetric but its wave function changes sign across a sphere. Density vanishes on that surface.

Distinguish a true node from sampling noise by reading the gold curve and resampling. Individual dots move between runs, but zero radial density stays at the same radius. Colors either side of the sphere also record the change of amplitude sign.

$$ R_{20}(r)\propto(2-r/a_0)e^{-r/(2a_0)} $$

+++ A closer look · A node in projection
Looking through the entire cloud superposes front and back points, which can fill a gap in the projection. Check the radial distribution.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Switch to 2s|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.thuThach.de: Choose 2s and drag r to its nodal sphere within 0.12a₀.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.thuThach.goiY: Find the positive zero of 2 − r/a₀.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.noiDung:
In a vertical 2p orbital the amplitude changes sign across the horizontal plane through the nucleus. Colors show the signs. Rotate the cloud to see both lobes share a center.

Choose a well-populated radius and look along and across the axis. The angular node is the whole horizontal plane, so it cuts every sphere centred on the nucleus. At the same radius, horizontal directions therefore have almost no dots, while directions along the axis have many. Find the plane separating the colors.

$$ Y_{10}(\theta,\phi)\propto\cos\theta $$

+++ A closer look · Angular probability
At the equatorial plane the cosine of the polar angle vanishes. Near the poles, probability per unit solid angle is larger.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[View 2p orbital|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.noiDung:
The orbitals share n and thus the same energy in the ideal Coulomb potential. Their angular distributions and radial nodes remain distinguishable.

Switch back and forth. The energy readout stays fixed even as the curve and cloud change. Energy alone is insufficient to select one of the two pictures; an additional measurement sensitive to direction or radius can distinguish them.

> [Con số] The energy of hydrogen is Eₙ = −13.6 eV/n². The 1s state lies at −13.6 eV; 2s and 2p both lie at −3.4 eV. The ladder at the corner of the table draws these levels, with the current one lit. Lifting the electron from 1s to n = 2 takes 10.2 eV, matching an ultraviolet photon of wavelength about 122 nm (the Lyman-alpha line).

$$ E_n/E_1=1/n^2 $$

+++ A closer look · Model assumptions
Fine structure, spin interactions and quantum-electrodynamic corrections are omitted. Precision measurements resolve small splittings outside this model.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Toggle 2s and 2p|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.noiDung:
For 2p the radial density initially rises and then decays exponentially. Its peak identifies which equal-thickness shells receive the most detections.

Imagine sorting detections into radial bins of equal thickness. The bin around the peak collects the most marks, yet any one mark may lie near the core or far past the peak. The peak characterizes repeated measurements rather than an individual particle’s orbital radius.

$$ P_{2p}(r)\propto r^4e^{-r/a_0} $$

+++ A closer look · Peak and tail
The maximum occurs at four Bohr radii. Larger measured radii still have nonzero probability.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Show the 2p radial curve|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.de: In 2p drag to the radial maximum within 0.15a₀.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.goiY: Balance the r⁴ factor against the decaying exponential.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.noiDung:
Check colors, axis orientation and sampling before comparing images. A surface of constant density looks different from a cloud of repeated detections.

Keeping only points in a thin slice loses much angular information; keeping only radii discards direction entirely. These reductions answer different questions. Describe what is discarded in going from the three-dimensional cloud to the one-dimensional gold curve.

> [Tóm lại] Each orbital has a principal quantum number n and an orbital quantum number l (s means l = 0, p means l = 1). The number of radial nodes is n − l − 1, the number of angular nodes is l, n − 1 in total. So 1s has no node, 2s has one spherical node, 2p has one planar node. The 2p orbital on the table is 2pz, with m = 0.

$$ \int_0^\infty P(r)\,dr=1 $$

+++ A closer look · Inverse question
Among these three states, a spherical cloud with a missing radial shell suggests 2s. A planar node suggests 2p.
+++

bai.baiGiang.congThuc.3.y: E₁ ≈ −13.6 eV; 2s and 2p both lie at −3.4 eV.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.4.y: Number of radial nodes and of angular nodes.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.hoi: Where does the 1s radial distribution peak?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.giai: The peak of r² exp(−2r/a₀) is at a₀.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.hoi: Which state has a radial node at r = 2a₀?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.hoi: What do the two colors of 2p signify?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.giai: Density is the squared magnitude of a single wave function.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.hoi: A hydrogen electron drops from 2p to 1s. How much energy does the emitted photon carry?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.giai: The difference of the two levels: −3.4 − (−13.6) = 10.2 eV. 3.4 eV is the ionization energy from level 2, and 13.6 eV the ionization energy from 1s.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.hoi: Why does radial density vanish at r = 0?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.dap: The area factor r² vanishes even though local 1s density is finite.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.6.hoi: Which quantity do 2s and 2p share in the ideal Coulomb potential?
